subject: ENGINEERING
title: Simply supported beam — determination of Young's modulus E
aim: Measure mid-span deflection of a simply supported beam under loading and unloading and determine Young's modulus E from the slope of δ against load W.

hazards.name: Falling slotted masses
hazards.text: Place masses gently onto the hanger without impact and stay clear of the load path.

apparatus.name: Dial deflection gauge on magnetic stand
Vernier caliper / micrometer
apparatus.spec: beam breadth b and depth d

procedure: Select the beam material and knife-edge span L, then mount the beam symmetrically on the supports.
Position the dial gauge plunger at mid-span and zero the dial bezel before adding load.
Add slotted masses in equal increments, waiting for the dial gauge needle to settle before recording each loading deflection.
Remove masses in reverse order and record unloading deflections to check elastic recovery and compute the mean deflection.
Plot mean deflection δ against load W and compute E = L³ / (48 I · slope).

precautions.text: Zeroed the dial gauge after mounting the beam and hanger before loading.
Waited for the dial gauge needle to settle after applying each mass gently without shock.
Recorded both loading and unloading readings to average out friction and check elastic behaviour.

glossary.second moment of area: Geometric stiffness property of a rectangular section, I = b d³ / 12.
glossary.young's modulus: Ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain within the elastic limit.
glossary.elastic limit: Maximum load a beam can carry and still return to zero deflection on unloading.
